b01.why: 'a man sold the Eiffel Tower': Lustig strolls in and offers an open palm toward the distant tower on the right, like a salesman presenting stock; slow push builds the hook

'Not a model. Not a ticket.': front-on shrug dismisses a toy tower popping on his right, then a paper ticket on his left; the slow pan left carries the eye from the first denial to the second, on the voice
'The actual tower.': pull back from Lustig to reveal the real iron base filling the right third; the smaller presenting figure sells the scale of the lie

b02.why: 'he got away with it': smug Lustig strides right with the suitcase of cash past the tower he never delivered, a few notes fluttering behind him; camera pans to follow the getaway

b03.why: 'he conned Al Capone': Lustig's offering palm faces a scowling, arms-crossed Capone across a wad of cash; push-in tightens the danger
'escaped a federal jail': hunched, shushing Lustig sneaks right past the wall, cuffs dropped behind him; camera pans with the escape
'was sent to Alcatraz': cuffs snap down onto a slumped, striped Lustig as the camera pulls back to isolate him on the fogged rock; the first downbeat in the hook

b04.caption: Victor Lustig
b04.why: 'His name was Victor Lustig': calm, hands-behind-back portrait framed against the hotel window and the lit tower; a slow sideways drift lets the name caption sit like a formal introduction without spending a push

'his whole trick fit inside one sentence': Lustig slides in on the right, flipped, and raises a single index finger, one finger for one sentence; the locked camera keeps the count clean and hands the number to the 'One sentence.' card

b05.why: 'you will know the sentence': flash-forward to the salon, Lustig in his ministry tailcoat standing over a seated, arms-folded dealer as if about to speak; the pull drags us out of the room before a word is heard, so the sentence stays a promise (new information: the disguise and the mark, not another tower pitch)

'why it works on ...everyone': a row of marks pops in one by one (greedy, shocked, sheepish) as the camera pans right along them, the pan landing on a last arms-crossed man who sets up the 'almost' in the next shot

'almost everyone': reverse angle on the holdout, Lustig strolls up to the one arms-crossed man and gives an open-palmed 'what can you do' shrug; the push onto his smirk ends the hook on the 'almost', a question the video promises to answer

needed_poses.desc: Al Capone stick figure in the same hand-drawn ink style (white round head, long black stick limbs): grey pinstripe double-breasted suit, white fedora with black band, cigar in mouth, arms crossed, heavy scowl with one eyebrow down; standing front-on, slight right turn; full body on flat magenta background

Victor Lustig (navy double-breasted coat, cream scarf, orange pocket square, black flat cap) climbing down a knotted bedsheet rope, both hands gripping the rope, legs wrapped, sly grin looking back over shoulder; facing right; full body on flat magenta background

Victor Lustig in black-and-white striped prison uniform and no cap, shoulders slumped, head bowed, hands cuffed in front, sad downturned mouth and drooping eyebrows; standing front-on; full body on flat magenta background
Victor Lustig dressed as a French ministry official: black tailcoat, top hat, white gloves, tricolour sash, holding a leather briefcase, chin up, solemn official expression, facing right
1920s Paris scrap-metal businessman stick figure (grey three-piece suit, flat cap, thick moustache), seated on a chair facing right, arms folded, sceptical squint

needed_plates.desc: 1920s Chicago street at night, hand-drawn ink and watercolour style matching the Paris plates: brick buildings with fire escapes, neon-less painted speakeasy sign, a parked black 1920s sedan at far right (x 80-100%), lamp posts at x ~12% and ~88%, wet asphalt from y ~63% down fully open, centre x 20-80% clear for two actors

Exterior of a 1930s New York federal detention building at night, same ink style: tall grey stone wall with barred windows, one window at upper-left open with a knotted white bedsheet rope hanging down to the street, searchlight beam across a navy sky, sidewalk from y ~63% down open, centre and right clear for a sneaking actor

Alcatraz island prison seen from the shore/dock in heavy grey fog, same ink style: cellhouse and lighthouse on the rock at right (x 60-95%), choppy grey bay water mid-ground, wooden dock planks foreground from y ~65% down fully open, left/centre clear for one actor; mood bleak and lonely

Palatial hotel salon interior: gilded panelled walls, two crystal chandeliers, tall mirrors, red velvet chairs pushed to the edges, polished parquet floor open y 66-100% full width, centre clear for 2-3 standing figures
